Helm v2 · LCD-5 · phases 1 + 2

This is the first physical build.

The firmware builds in CI, but has never run on a real board. The case has not been printed. Drawings here are schematic, not to scale. A checked box records your work, not a certified result.

0.2

Put the tools within reach

No extra parts
IronCalipersMultimeter
  • Soldering iron and solder, for the headers. The iron also sets inserts.
  • Flush cutters and wire strippers.
  • 2 mm hex key for the M3 button head screws; the knob’s own set-screw key.
  • 3D printer for PETG, plus calipers for the fit checks.
  • Multimeter for continuity and voltage checks.
  • Optional: insert tip and USB power meter.
Prepare the work surface.

Keep the unpowered board on a clean, nonconductive surface. Keep loose metal away from it. Handle boards by their edges, keep fingers off contacts, and disconnect both USB cables before changing wiring.

Not in the repo yet

A static-safe workstation procedure, iron temperature, soldering technique, ventilation setup, and your printer’s PETG temperatures are not specified. Use the instructions for your tools before the hands-on steps. Do not improvise those settings.

Source: Parts list · Wiring

0.3

Learn the five bench basics

BreadboardHeaders
Meter

Breadboard rows

Some holes are joined inside. A shared row joins wires without solder; rails distribute power. The exact row map and rail breaks are not in the repo yet. Check your board’s diagram or continuity before wiring.

Header pins

A male pin plugs into a female socket. The LCD-5 header is expected to be female. Parts get soldered male headers, then sit on the breadboard. A header pin number and a GPIO number are different labels.

The multimeter

Continuity checks a connection with power disconnected. DC voltage checks a powered circuit against GND. Never use continuity on a powered board. Jack selection and range depend on your meter; follow its manual.

Data vs power

A cable that lights the screen may still fail to carry data. Both USB-C cables must be data-capable. The two sockets have different jobs: flashing and the Helm link.

Polarity and direction

5V, 3V3, and GND are not interchangeable. VIN is the knob’s power input. Light data enters I or DIN and leaves O. A and C are the key switch’s anode and cathode: A goes to its GPIO, C to GND.

Correct

Match each pad’s printed label.

Wrong

Do not assume the second row is a mirror.

0.4

Set aside the printed-build supplies

Phase 2 kit
Parts check
  • x10 M3 x 4 mm heat-set inserts (Adafruit 4255, one 50-pack).
  • x1 pad 1.6 mm adhesive neoprene foam, about 100 x 40 mm, plus scraps.
  • About 60 g + 150 g PETG, estimates for the small parts and test enclosure. White or natural for the light holder; black or grey for the others.
  • A few cm VHB tape or epoxy. Use VHB for removable test holders.
  • x10 M3 x 6 mm screws: four cradle, six closure. The BOM lists these in phase 3, but the printed enclosure needs them now.
  • CA glue for the locating tabs. Assembly specifies it; the BOM does not give a quantity.
For a complete enclosed fit check

The fit step also references parts listed under phase 3: x1 Adafruit 6153 back jack, x1 4090 breakout, x1 6370 ribbon, x4 feet (550), female-male jumpers (1954, BOM use about 12), and a 1609 Perma-Proto for the later soldered power distribution.

You can test their physical clearance here. The soldered harness is a separate prerequisite for a complete powered, closed-case test. Its construction stays in the existing assembly and wiring docs.

Bench build

Screen first. Then the link, knob, lights, keys, and chime.

02 / 06
Use a terminal at the repository root.

Commands below come from the build docs. Replace /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX with the flashing port and /dev/cu.usbmodemYYYY with the native link port. They are placeholders, not discovered devices. Keep a note of each name.

1.1

Build the firmware first

No extra parts
Mac + terminal

Install ESP-IDF v5.5.6. Use the same python3 for installation and export. You can do this before the board arrives.

Terminal · repository root 
git clone -b v5.5.6 --depth 1 --recursive --shallow-submodules https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git ~/.cache/helm-esp-idf/esp-idf-v5.5.6
IDF_TOOLS_PATH=~/.cache/helm-esp-idf/tools ~/.cache/helm-esp-idf/esp-idf-v5.5.6/install.sh esp32p4

Success: The ESP32-P4 tools finish installing without an error.

Terminal · repository root 
IDF_TOOLS_PATH=~/.cache/helm-esp-idf/tools . ~/.cache/helm-esp-idf/esp-idf-v5.5.6/export.sh
idf.py -C firmware/idf build

Success: The firmware build completes. Its first run downloads the board package and LVGL into firmware/idf/managed_components/.

Not in the repo yet

A first-time Mac setup walkthrough for Git, Python, and terminal use is not provided. If a prerequisite is missing, resolve that before flashing.

If this checkout previously built the 4 inch board

The firmware README requires clearing the old managed components and sdkconfig before the first LCD-5 build. Follow its Build section; do not reuse a v1 configuration.

Source: Firmware · Assembly

1.2

Power the board. Flash. Touch.

LCD-5 x1Data cable x1
Terminal

First real-hardware test: note what you see

  1. Leave the expansion header empty. Read the silkscreen beside the two USB-C sockets.
  2. List ports before and after plugging USB TO UART into the Mac. It is nearer RESET, BOOT, and POWER. If dark, press POWER once and record that it needed a press.
Terminal · repository root 
ls /dev/cu.*

Success: A new serial port appears after connection. The CH343P name and whether a WCH driver is needed on macOS are unverified.

Terminal · repository root 
esptool.py --chip esp32p4 -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX chip_id
esptool.py --chip esp32p4 -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash_id

Success: A chip revision is reported; flash should read 32 MB. Record both before choosing a build.

Chip older than v3.0? Use this separate build
Terminal · repository root 
idf.py -C firmware/idf -B build/idf-rev1 -D SDKCONFIG="$PWD/build/idf-rev1/sdkconfig" \
  -D "SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS=sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.p4-rev1" build

Success: The older-silicon build completes in its own directory.

For this board, add -B build/idf-rev1 -D SDKCONFIG="$PWD/build/idf-rev1/sdkconfig" to every later idf.py command. Use this flash command:

Terminal · repository root 
idf.py -C firmware/idf -B build/idf-rev1 -D SDKCONFIG="$PWD/build/idf-rev1/sdkconfig" -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor

Success: Flashing completes and the monitor shows boot logs. Exit with Ctrl+].

For the normal build:

Terminal · repository root 
idf.py -C firmware/idf -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor

Success: Flashing completes and boot logs appear. The screen should show “link unknown”. Exit the monitor with Ctrl+].

If esptool waits at “power-on sync”, hold BOOT and press RESET. The expected automatic reset is still untested on a board.

Prop the module glass up, USB-C edge left. Default rotation is 270 (90 counter-clockwise). Tap the corners and on-screen keys: touch should land under your finger.

Changing a firmware setting
Terminal · repository root 
idf.py -C firmware/idf menuconfig

Success: The configuration menu opens. Helm settings are under Helm deck.

Use the step 1.2 build flags for older silicon. Save the setting, rebuild with the matching build command, and flash that build again. A menu change alone does not update the board.

Source: Assembly · Firmware · Wiring

1.3

Connect the link socket

Flashed LCD-5Data cables x2
Mac

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Keep the flashing cable connected. Plug the second cable into USB, nearer the header. Both cables together are expected to be fine: each supplies power through its own ideal diode.

A new /dev/cu.usbmodem* appears, a CDC-ACM device named Helm deck. This is the bridge port. Then unplug USB TO UART and check that USB alone powers the board.

Correct

Plug seated in the labelled socket.

Wrong

A loose plug or power-only cable can hide the link.

Source: Assembly · Wiring · Firmware

1.4

Let the Mac talk to Helm

DeckNative USB link
Terminal

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Start in dry run, the default. The bridge logs notes and pane focus instead of sending them.

Terminal · repository root 
python3 -m helm.bridge --port /dev/cu.usbmodemYYYY -v

Success: Look for device hello: fw=helm-idf-0.1 caps=screen-1280x720,... . A model should appear within 2 s.

Stop the bridge and wait: the deck should say “no word from the bridge for 10 s”. Restart it for the remaining tests.

Optional: start the bridge at login

Only after the board’s port stays stable:

Terminal · repository root 
scripts/install-agent.sh --port /dev/cu.usbmodemYYYY

Success: The login agent installs using the same link port in dry run.

After the dry-run actions behave and you trust them, this enables real notes and pane focus:

Terminal · repository root 
scripts/install-agent.sh --port /dev/cu.usbmodemYYYY --live

Success: The login agent installs in live mode. Notes and pane focus are now real actions.

See the login-agent documentation for the complete workflow.

Source: Assembly · Firmware

1.5

Add the knob and light bar

5880 + knob x1Stick x1BreadboardHeaders + jumpers
Iron + cuttersSet-screw keyMeter

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Unplug both USB cables.

The header’s 5V rail stays live whenever either cable is connected, even when POWER is off. Disconnect again before each wiring change.

  1. Find J3 pin 1 at the end away from the USB sockets. Odd pins are the edge row, even pins the inner row. Wire by silkscreen, never by a Raspberry Pi pinout.
  2. With power disconnected, check GND to a USB-C shell in continuity mode: it should beep. Pin 1 to the shell should stay silent.
  3. Solder extra-long headers to the encoder’s labelled breakout pads and the stick’s input pads: DIN, 5VDC, GND. Put them on the breadboard.
  4. Use male-male wires: pin 1 / 5V to the red rail, pin 5 / GND to the blue rail. Check your breadboard’s rail breaks.
Correct

Knob VIN to 3V3, pin 2.

Wrong

Never connect knob VIN to 5V.

The stick gets 5VDC to the red rail, GND to the blue rail, and DIN to pin 15 / GPIO21 for now. Confirm the encoder’s shaft is the expected 6 mm D-shaft, fit the knob and tighten its set screw. The vendor drawings disagree about the shaft; do not force a mismatched knob.

Reconnect both cables, then open the log:

Terminal · repository root 
idf.py -C firmware/idf -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX monitor

Success: Expect “seesaw hardware 0x87, product 4991”. Exit with Ctrl+]. Older silicon needs the step 1.2 build flags here too.

Clockwise should move down the list, one step per detent; press opens. A 0.8 s press mutes and the knob’s light goes red. If direction is reversed, use Helm deck > Knob (Adafruit 5880 I2C encoder) > Reverse the turn direction.

Until the keys join the chain, the first four key colors land on the stick’s first four LEDs. That is expected. Flicker is not: see troubleshooting.

Source: Assembly · Wiring · Firmware

1.6

Add the four keys

NeoKeys x4Switches + caps x4Headers + jumpers
Iron + cuttersMeter

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Disconnect both USB cables again.

Keep header pin 8 / GPIO2 empty. It may carry the touch interrupt. YES belongs on pin 17 / GPIO22.

Solder both five-pin rows on each NeoKey for strength. Read the labels on each row. Seat the Kailh switches, then caps marked YES, LATER, HOLD, SHOW ME. A dot of hot glue is suggested in the assembly docs if a switch works loose.

On each NeoKey, connect VDD to 5V, and both GND and C to ground. Connect A as follows:

YESpin 17GPIO22
LATERpin 12GPIO3
HOLDpin 14GPIO4
SHOW MEpin 11GPIO5

Move the light data wire from the stick to YES I, then join the chain:

Reconnect power. No rebuild is needed; GPIO keys are on by default and touch still works. Keep the bridge in dry run.

  1. Select an item with the knob. Only applicable actions should light.
  2. Press and release SHOW ME. The bridge should log a pane focus.
  3. Hold YES. Confirm fills for 1 s. Release early: nothing is sent. Hold past 1 s: the bridge logs the note it would send and the deck shows Result.
  4. With the key held, measure DC voltage between A and GND: expect about 0.6 to 0.7 V, the diode drop. If a press is missed, tell the firmware maintainer before changing wiring.

Source: Assembly · Wiring · Firmware

1.7

Add the chime. Live with the bench build.

Boxed speaker x1
CalipersListen + observe

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Disconnect power, then plug the included 8 ohm, 2 W speaker into SPK, a latching GH1.25 connector. Reconnect and let something new arrive with the bridge running. A long knob press mutes.

Source conflict: chime volume

Assembly 1.7 and the firmware README give a default volume of 60. Wiring check 14 says to start at 30. The guide does not treat either as a measured loudness result. Check the setting under Helm deck > Chime > Volume and record what you test.

Listen for a sensible level, quiet between chimes, and two distinct tones when two arrive. Measure the speaker’s width, depth, and height for the worksheet.

Phase 1 exit: a week of daily use on the bench. Stay in dry run first; use live mode only once it behaves.

Print the fit coupon

print_mx_coupon.stl x1SwitchEncoder
PrinterCalipers

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Download the coupon STL. Print plate on the bed, rim up, no supports, in PETG. Use 0.2 mm layers, 3 walls, 20 percent infill.

Try a switch in each square and the encoder bushing in each round hole. Record which seats without forcing. Dots identify the holes: 1 to 4 below for the keys, 1 or 2 above for the knob.

A printer check, not a metal decision.

Printers often make holes 0.1 to 0.2 mm small. The later metal coupon decides final hole sizes. Do not treat this print as proof of laser-cut fit.

Not in the repo yet

No nozzle/bed temperatures, print speeds, cooling settings, support interface settings, or heat-set iron temperature are given. Use your filament, printer, and insert supplier’s guidance.

The cover is 139.6 x 143.7 mm; the base is 145.0 x 135.7 mm. Both fit a 256 x 256 mm bed as single pieces. Check your own bed and slicer preview. The base’s service-slot top is a 33 mm sloped bridge; sag there affects cable clearance.

  1. Match your insert supplier’s hole recommendation to the 4.0 mm printed holes. Adafruit 4255 lists 4.2 mm outside diameter, but its required hole size is unverified. Stop if the recommendation is unknown.
  2. Heat-set x4 M3 inserts into the cradle legs from below. The holes are 6.5 mm deep.
  3. Heat-set x6 M3 x 4 inserts into the test-cover flanges from below, flush with their underside. Flanges are 4.4 mm thick; inserts must not be longer.
  4. Push the x5 tabs in from the cradle’s top, glass side toward the middle. Each shoulder sits on its arm; secure with a drop of CA glue.

Source: Assembly · Parts list · Case notes

Fit and measure

This is the sizing test. Measure the real parts before ordering metal.

04 / 06

The print is a question.
Your parts are the answer.

Check that each part fits without force, then record the actual dimensions. A CAD clearance check cannot tell you how the real glass, cables, and switches feel.

How to use this worksheet

Work in mm. Measure from the named reference surface. Write the actual reading and your fit observation, including a mismatch. Entries save locally when browser storage is available; download a copy before moving or replacing this file.

2.3

Fit the deck in the printed enclosure

Printed cover + baseModule + cradle + foamKeys x4Encoder + knobStick + holderSpeaker + holderJack + breakout + ribbonM3 x 6 screws x10
2 mm hex + knob keyCalipers

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Keep power disconnected while fitting.

This is a physical fit test. Do not trap the breadboard inside. A complete closed-case electrical test requires the in-case harness referenced by assembly 2.3; construction of that soldered harness is outside this guide. Mark any dependent check “not tested”.

  1. Base. Put the 1.6 mm foam pad on the cradle. Attach its four legs to the floor with x4 M3 x 6 screws from below. Confirm all five locating tabs are seated.
  2. Controls. Press switches into the cover from the front; NeoKeys attach from inside. Left to right: YES, LATER, HOLD, SHOW ME. Fit the caps. Mount the encoder bushing from inside, nut on top; fit the knob and check it clears the nut.
  3. Light and sound. Place the stick LEDs toward the diffuser, DIN toward the keys, to the left. The holder’s tongue seats in the 49 x 6 mm window. Centre the speaker holder under its slots. Use removable VHB for these test bonds.
  4. Cable space. Check the back jack’s flange outside and nut inside, slot horizontal. Trial-position the 4090 on foam tape under the module’s left half, receptacle facing left. Assembly locates it about 66 mm from the front and 12 mm from the left wall. If its unmodified lead prevents seating, leave the jack check incomplete and use the linked harness instructions later.
  5. Module. Place it glass up between the tabs, USB edge left. Trial-fit the 6370 ribbon to the breakout and the native USB socket, nearer the back. It drops beside the module before turning underneath. Do not pinch it or the speaker lead.
  6. Before closing. Once wiring is ready, test native USB power-on while POWER is reachable. If it needs a press, stop and report it to the case maintainer. POWER is inaccessible with the cover on. Disconnect power again before adjusting or closing.
  7. Close gently. Lower the cover between the base’s side walls. Glass meets the underside of the face; foam takes up tolerance. Use x6 M3 x 6 screws from below into the flange inserts. Stop if closing forces the glass, cables, or parts. Feet, if fitted, go clear of screw heads.
Good fit is observable.

Switches clip firmly. Knob turns without rubbing the nut. Glass sits firmly without bowing or sliding. Light reads through the window. Speaker sits sealed under the slots. Both USB-C cables seat, with the flashing cable entering through the service slot. Use it in the print for a while once the complete harness works.

Source: Assembly · Case notes · Wiring

2.4

Measure every assumption

Fitted test enclosureActual bought parts
CalipersFit + touch check

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Targets are assumptions, not pass bands.

The repo does not specify measurement tolerances for most entries below. A small numerical difference is not automatically a pass. If a reading differs or the physical check fails, record it, update the relevant case parameter with the case maintainer, rebuild and reprint affected parts before metal. Do not force a part to match the drawing.

For dimensions, use calipers on the unpowered parts. Inspect glass and touch clearance gently; do not put metal jaws against a powered board. A thread’s pitch cannot be established from outside diameter alone: verify the encoder thread against its documentation as well.

Source: Assembly · Case notes

Your measurement record

Each row records an observation. Blank means unmeasured.

01

USB receptacle centres

Repo assumption
26.4 / 44.3 mm from the front glass edge in case notes. Assembly lists 26.36 / 44.31 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers; module held as mounted, USB edge left. Measure from the front glass edge to the centre of each receptacle.

Good physical result
Both cables seat through the service slot without bearing on its edges.

MODULE_PCB_INSET_V, MODULE_USB_UART, MODULE_USB_NATIVE

If it differs or fails
Service-slot position and ribbon plug. Assembly calls this MODULE_USB_CENTRES; that name differs from the case notes. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

02

Glass to USB centre

Repo assumption
Source conflict: case notes 9.3 mm; assembly 2.4 says 6.0 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers; measure perpendicular from the glass face to each receptacle centre.

Good physical result
The slot lines up in depth and neither cable lifts the module.

MODULE_USB_DEPTH

If it differs or fails
Service-slot depth. Do not choose a conflicting number without measuring. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

03

Header and jumper clearance

Repo assumption
Rows 3.1 / 5.6 mm from PCB edge; socket 5.1 mm proud; 20 mm for plugs and wire bend below.

Measure with / from
Calipers; measure socket position and height, then the actual fitted jumper housings and bend space.

Good physical result
Cradle clears the socket and plugs; wires are not crushed when the cover closes.

HEADER_ROWS_IN, HEADER_HEIGHT, HEADER_PLUGS

If it differs or fails
Cradle back edge and wiring clearance. A full wire-routing model is not provided. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

04

Boxed speaker

Repo assumption
Source conflict: case notes and BOM assume 30 x 20 x 6.8 mm; assembly lists 30 x 20 x 5 mm for an Adafruit speaker.

Measure with / from
Calipers; measure the speaker that actually came with the LCD-5, width x depth x height. Check its lead reaches SPK.

Good physical result
Fits its holder and sits sealed under the slots, without loading the face.

SPEAKER_BOX

If it differs or fails
Speaker holder. The boxed speaker size and lead length are not published in these docs. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

05

Screen window

Repo assumption
111.8 x 63.8 mm; lit viewing area 110.32 x 62.28 mm in case notes.

Measure with / from
Calipers for the opening; eyes and touch for the installed, powered screen after safe assembly.

Good physical result
Lit area framed without black border showing; face does not press the touch area; touch still lands correctly.

SCREEN_WINDOW_X, SCREEN_WINDOW_V

If it differs or fails
Face window. No additional numerical acceptance range is specified. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

06

Module thickness

Repo assumption
11.6 mm in assembly 2.4.

Measure with / from
Calipers; glass face to the tallest component on the back.

Good physical result
Cradle supports the module without a component taking an unintended load.

MODULE_THICKNESS

If it differs or fails
Module fit. Record what the tallest component is as well as its height. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

07

Cradle and foam

Repo assumption
3 mm cradle plate; 1.6 mm supplied foam, assumed 1.5 mm compressed.

Measure with / from
Calipers on accessible parts; inspect the assembled fit without squeezing the glass to obtain a reading.

Good physical result
Module sits firmly against the face, no bowing and no sliding.

CRADLE_T, CRADLE_FOAM

If it differs or fails
Cradle leg length. Compression tolerance and a tightening torque are not in the repo yet. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

08

Five locating tabs

Repo assumption
0.5 mm glass gap; tab top 0.8 mm under the face.

Measure with / from
Calipers plus gentle trial fit. Inspect the module edge wherever each tab touches.

Good physical result
Glass drops between tabs without force; glass is the outermost edge at contact points; tabs stay in their slots.

CRADLE_TAB_GAP, CRADLE_TAB_TOP

If it differs or fails
Tab positions. Slot retention with CA glue is untested. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

09

Encoder bushing

Repo assumption
M7 x 0.75; model hole 7.5 mm. Coupon offers 7.2 / 7.5 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers for bushing diameter and length; confirm thread from the part documentation. Inspect for an anti-rotation tab.

Good physical result
Bushing seats; nut engages and holds; any anti-rotation tab has clearance.

ENCODER_HOLE

If it differs or fails
Knob hole. If an anti-rotation tab exists, the case needs a matching hole before proceeding. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

10

Encoder body

Repo assumption
13.4 x 12.5 mm; plate-to-PCB height 6.5 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers; measure body footprint and distance from plate to PCB.

Good physical result
Body and PCB clear the adjacent parts with the cover closed.

ENCODER_BODY, ENCODER_BODY_HEIGHT

If it differs or fails
Internal clearance. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

11

NeoKey stack

Repo assumption
13.0 mm plate top to lowest wire; PCB thickness 1.6 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers with switch fitted: measure from the plate top to the lowest wire, plus PCB thickness.

Good physical result
Switch clips in firmly; boards and wires clear the floor.

KEY_STACK_DEPTH, NEOKEY_PCB_THICKNESS

If it differs or fails
Front clearance. Measure with real wires fitted, not just the bare PCB. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

12

Keycaps

Repo assumption
Model 17.6 mm square x 5.0 mm high; fit check also covers 18.6 mm square x 14 mm high.

Measure with / from
Calipers on your chosen caps; press each fitted cap through its travel.

Good physical result
Caps do not collide, rub, or bottom out improperly. The larger envelope is a model check, not hardware proof.

KEYCAP, KEYCAP_HEIGHT

If it differs or fails
Spacing check and renders. OEM backlit caps are taller than the flat render. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

13

Knob and nut

Repo assumption
24 mm flange; source conflict: DROK height 14.5 mm in BOM and case notes, 11 mm in assembly 2.4.

Measure with / from
Calipers for diameter and height; inspect recess depth, nut clearance, and actual shaft type.

Good physical result
Knob fits the shaft, turns freely, and its flange hides the nut.

KNOB_D, KNOB_HEIGHT

If it differs or fails
Spacing and renders. Recess depth is not listed. If it does not cover the nut, record the mismatch before choosing a replacement. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

14

LED span and stick

Repo assumption
Window 49 x 6 mm; stick thickness with LEDs 3.2 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers for LED span and total board-plus-LED height; inspect the lit diffuser.

Good physical result
Stick seats without pressure on LEDs; light reads through the window with DIN toward the keys.

LIGHT_WINDOW, LIGHT_STICK_THICKNESS

If it differs or fails
Window and holder pocket. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

15

Flashing cable plug body

Repo assumption
12.35 x 6.5 mm assumed.

Measure with / from
Calipers across the widest parts of your cable overmold. Test seating through the service slot.

Good physical result
Plug fully seats in USB TO UART without catching the slot.

USB_PLUG_OVERMOLD

If it differs or fails
Service-slot size. A matching connector type does not guarantee a matching plug body. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

16

6370 ribbon plug head

Repo assumption
12 x 7.3 mm; stands 3.5 mm out of the receptacle, estimated.

Measure with / from
Calipers on the head, then measure how far it protrudes when seated. Trial-route its turn under the module.

Good physical result
Head clears the wall, leaves the other port usable, and the ribbon routes without being trapped.

RIBBON_PLUG_HEAD, MODULE_X

If it differs or fails
Module-to-left-wall distance. Ribbon turn is simplified in the model. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

17

4090 receptacle height

Repo assumption
4.2 mm centre height above the board underside.

Measure with / from
Calipers; measure from PCB underside to receptacle centre. Include the actual mounting tape in the fit trial.

Good physical result
Ribbon plug clears the floor and fully seats.

BREAKOUT_USB_HEIGHT

If it differs or fails
Ribbon-to-floor clearance. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

18

6153 jack lead bundle

Repo assumption
3.5 mm bundle assumed.

Measure with / from
Calipers lightly across the six-wire bundle; trial-route without squeezing it.

Good physical result
Lead clears neighbouring parts and is not pinched at closure.

BACK_JACK_LEAD_D

If it differs or fails
Clearance only. Full lead routing is not modelled. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

19

Heat-set insert holes

Repo assumption
4.0 mm printed holes; 4255 insert outside diameter 4.2 mm.

Measure with / from
Calipers for the actual printed hole; compare with the insert supplier’s required hole size.

Good physical result
Insert seats and holds without splitting or distorting the part.

PRINT_INSERT_D

If it differs or fails
Cradle legs and printed flange fit. Recommended hole size for 4255 is not in the repo yet. Record the difference; review the parameter, rebuild, and repeat the affected fit check.

Deferred assumption: metal flange nut

The case notes also assume an S-M3-0 nut outside diameter of 6.0 mm, absent from the catalog. Printed flanges use inserts instead. Record it as not tested in phases 1 and 2; it remains a clearance check before metal.

When a measurement changes the design

The docs direct you to update case/helm_case/params.py, then follow assembly 2.5 to rebuild and test the case. Reprint every affected part. This guide does not change the model or validate an order.

What comes next

Once the bench build and measurements are complete: phase 3 covers the metal coupon, metal order, engraving, soldered wiring, and final assembly. Read the case’s remaining unverified items before any order. A printed fit does not verify bends, finish, or bonded holders on anodized aluminum.

When it does not work

Find the symptom. Check the simplest boundary. Record the result.

05 / 06
Change one thing at a time.

Record the symptom first. Disconnect both USB cables before rewiring, moving headers, or reseating parts. POWER alone does not remove the header’s 5V. Causes below are candidates from the verification lists, not diagnoses.

T.1

Power, flashing, and the link

LCD-5Data cables
TerminalOptional USB power meter

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Dark board after plugging in
Likely cause
The power latch may need a POWER press; start-on-USB is unverified.
Check
Use the board alone. Check each port alone, then both. Note whether POWER is needed.
Fix / next action
Press POWER once for the bench check. If required, stop before closing the case and tell the case maintainer.
No new serial port
Likely cause
Wrong socket, cable without data, or unverified CH343P driver behavior.
Check
Compare serial-port listings before and after connecting. Read USB vs USB TO UART on the silkscreen.
Fix / next action
Use a known data-capable cable in the intended socket. A macOS WCH-driver procedure is not in the repo yet; do not guess one.
Flash waits at “power-on sync”
Likely cause
Automatic reset through the CH343P did not work as expected.
Check
Confirm USB TO UART and the measured serial-port name.
Fix / next action
Hold BOOT and press RESET, as assembly 1.2 specifies. Record that automatic reset failed.
Firmware does not boot after flashing
Likely cause
Build may target the wrong silicon revision; flash size or PSRAM may differ.
Check
Read chip_id and flash_id. Expect 32 MB flash. The 200 MHz PSRAM setting is unverified on hardware.
Fix / next action
For pre-v3.0 silicon use the separate build in 1.2, including its flags when flashing. If flash size differs or PSRAM fails, save the log for the firmware maintainer.
Bridge starts, but no device hello
Likely cause
Bridge may be opening the flashing socket rather than native USB.
Check
Use the port discovered in 1.3. Expect hello and a model within 2 s; stopping the bridge should show the 10 s stale message.
Fix / next action
Point the bridge at USB. If native USB still misbehaves, the documented UART0 fallback is under Helm deck > Link to the Mac. It shares boot text and can reset when opened; see the firmware README before switching.
Works direct, fails through the back jack
Likely cause
The hand-soldered high-speed lead is an unverified weak point.
Check
Compare direct native USB with the complete jack path; test the Mac plug both ways up.
Fix / next action
Return to the direct cable to isolate the problem. The wiring docs call for a short lead, twisted D+ / D-, and checked joints. Harness repair belongs to those docs, outside this guide.
Power draw is unknown
Likely cause
The LCD-5 backlight’s board draw is not published.
Check
Use a USB power meter, if available, in the Mac cable.
Fix / next action
Record the actual reading. Keep the light brightness cap at 64/255 until measured. No total-current acceptance limit is specified in the repo.

Source: Wiring · Firmware · Case notes

T.2

Screen, touch, and timing

LCD-5
Touch + observeBoot log

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Picture is upside down
Likely cause
The assumed native panel orientation may differ.
Check
Hold the board glass up, USB edge left. Default rotation is 270.
Fix / next action
Choose 90 clockwise in Helm deck > Screen rotation, then rebuild and flash the correct chip-revision build.
Touch is absent or lands somewhere else
Likely cause
GT911 discovery or rotation mapping may be wrong.
Check
Look for “Touch 0x5d found” or “Touch 0x14 found”. Tap all four corners, a row, and each on-screen key.
Fix / next action
Record the mapping and log. Mirrored/swapped touch needs the firmware’s display_start flags checked; do not compensate by moving key wiring.
Touch triggers a YES action
Likely cause
Something may be on GPIO2, the optional touch interrupt.
Check
Inspect header pin 8. R108 may connect the GT911 interrupt there.
Fix / next action
With both USB cables removed, leave pin 8 empty and wire YES A to pin 17 / GPIO22.
Scrolling tears, Confirm freezes, or timing feels wrong
Likely cause
Rotated rendering and touch thresholds have not been tested on this board.
Check
Check a smooth 1 s Confirm fill, list scrolling, a 0.8 s long press, and swipes. Firmware specifies 48 px per swipe step and a 12 px drag threshold.
Fix / next action
Save observations for the firmware maintainer. The firmware notes suggest trying adapter PPA acceleration before changing display modes; that is an engineering investigation, not a wiring fix.
Deck stalls when the Mac is not reading
Likely cause
The USB send timeout may not behave as intended on hardware.
Check
Expected firmware behavior: a blocked frame drops after 100 ms, without stalling the deck. This is not a stopwatch measurement.
Fix / next action
Record a reproduction and logs for the firmware maintainer. A beginner timing-test procedure is not in the repo yet.

Source: Firmware · Wiring

T.3

Keys, knob, lights, and sound

KeysKnobLightsSpeaker
MultimeterLogObserve

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Key press is missed
Likely cause
A/C wiring or a diode voltage too high for a reliable low.
Check
A goes to its assigned GPIO, C and GND both go to ground. A held key should measure about 0.6 to 0.7 V from A to GND.
Fix / next action
If wiring matches and presses still fail, tell the firmware maintainer before changing the circuit. GPIO3 to 5 takeover from JTAG is also a hardware assumption.
Knob is not found
Likely cause
Power/bus wiring, address conflict, or no attached knob.
Check
Expect “seesaw hardware 0x87, product 4991” at 0x36 on GPIO7 SDA / GPIO8 SCL. Check VIN is 3V3. A camera can also answer at 0x36.
Fix / next action
Disconnect power and correct labelled connections. Use the no-camera board. Absence logs “no knob” once and retries every 2 s; touch should still work. Do not hot-plug just to test recovery.
Knob turns the wrong way or mute does not show
Likely cause
Direction setting or push/light behavior is unverified.
Check
One step per detent; a 0.8 s hold should mute and light the knob red.
Fix / next action
Use the Reverse the turn direction setting for backwards motion. Record missed pushes or absent mute indication for firmware investigation.
Wrong LEDs light or colors flicker
Likely cause
Chain order, I/O direction, GRB order, or marginal 3.3 V data into 5 V lights.
Check
Check GPIO21 → YES → LATER → HOLD → SHOW ME → stick. Data must enter I / DIN. Before keys are fitted, the stick receives the four key colors first.
Fix / next action
Correct direction/order with power disconnected. For first-light flicker, docs propose 3V3 chain power at low brightness or a 74AHCT125 level shifter. These are unverified alternatives; the stick is specified for 5 V (4 to 7 V), so do not treat 3V3 as a guaranteed solution. A level-shifter wiring procedure is not in the repo yet.
Key icons are hard to read in daylight
Likely cause
Cap diffusion and brightness have not been tested.
Check
Look through the actual caps at the default 64/255 cap. Only applicable keys light.
Fix / next action
Record readability and current draw before considering brightness changes. Printed paper legends and custom shine-through caps differ.
No chime, noisy idle, or two tones run together
Likely cause
Mute state, connector mismatch, speaker setting, or audio behavior.
Check
Use the boxed GH1.25 speaker in SPK, not a PicoBlade lookalike. Check mute and the Chime output/volume settings.
Fix / next action
Unmute, reseat with power removed, and retest. Report noise or merged tones. Default volume is 60 in firmware; wiring check 14 says 30. Record the value actually used.

Source: Wiring · Firmware

T.4

The printed enclosure does not fit

Printed enclosure + fitted parts
CalipersFit check

First real-hardware test: note what you see

Glass bows, moves, or catches a tab
Likely cause
Foam, cradle height, glass-edge assumptions, or tab fit differs.
Check
Measure the foam/cradle and tab worksheet entries. The glass must be outermost where tabs touch.
Fix / next action
Stop tightening. Remove the cover, record the interference, review the parameters and reprint. Do not force glass between tabs.
Cover will not close or a cable will not seat
Likely cause
Real wire routing or plug bodies exceed the simplified model.
Check
Check header housings, speaker lead, ribbon bend, back-jack lead, and service-slot sag.
Fix / next action
Record the obstruction and actual dimensions. Rework the case parameters/routing with the case maintainer, then repeat the fit test.
Walls warp, supports damage flanges, inserts do not hold
Likely cause
The test enclosure has never been printed; these features are unverified.
Check
Cover face down, supports under bottom flanges only; base floor down. Check insert supplier’s required hole size.
Fix / next action
Use the printer/filament guidance to correct print quality. Review PRINT_INSERT_D against the real inserts. Do not compensate with force or longer screws.
Holder comes loose or speaker does not seal
Likely cause
Test bond or real speaker size differs from the model.
Check
Check the speaker worksheet, holder seating, and VHB bond.
Fix / next action
Refit or revise the holder before powered use. A successful printed test does not verify bonding to anodized metal.

Source: Case notes · Assembly

How it works

A small physical interface to the work happening on your Mac.

06 / 06

One thing to notice.
One deliberate action.

The deck makes incoming work visible on your desk. Turn to browse, press to open, and hold a key when you mean to answer.

H.1

Know what each part does

ScreenKeys x4KnobBarChime
Read + identify
Screen
The 1280 x 720 landscape touch display shows status, items that need attention, detail, confirmation, and results. Touch gives you on-screen keys, swipe, tap, and long press even before the physical controls are fitted.
Four keys
YES, LATER, and HOLD are held answers with a 1 s confirmation bar; releasing early cancels. SHOW ME is a press-and-release action for pane focus. A key lights only when its action applies to the selected item.
Knob
Turn to move through items or text. Press to open or go back. Hold 0.8 s to mute. Its own red light means muted. Its encoder board talks over the same I2C bus as touch and audio, so VIN must stay on 3V3.
Light bar
The eight-light stick follows the four key lights in one data chain. It signals arrivals, unseen items, uncertain link/firstmate state, and usage when calm. With DIN facing the keys, its direction agrees with the firmware.
Chime
A short sound draws attention to a model that asks for it, unless muted. The included speaker uses the LCD-5’s audio amplifier through SPK, so it needs no expansion GPIO.
Reading the light language

Key colors: YES green, LATER blue, HOLD amber, SHOW ME white. While a key is held, only that key lights. The bar runs a green head left to right for 2 s after an arrival, is amber at 55% for unknown link/firstmate state, pulses unseen items between 55% and 100% every 1.4 s, and shows usage when calm. These percentages describe patterns under the separate 64/255 brightness cap.

Source: Firmware · Wiring

H.2

Know what runs on the Mac

HelmUSB link
Mac + firstmate
The bridge
A program on the Mac that sends the deck a model of what is happening, receives its actions, and logs or sends notes and pane focus. Native USB carries this link. The other port carries flashing and logs.
firstmate
The system on the Mac that the deck’s notes go to. The deck can show an answer as sent, then Seen once firstmate has read it, or warn that firstmate has not picked it up. Sending and being read are separate states.
Dry run
The same physical controls can be exercised while notes and focus actions are only logged. Use this to check early releases and long holds before enabling live behavior.
Not in the repo yet

The listed build sources do not provide a beginner firstmate installation or sample-work setup walkthrough. A working screen and USB hello prove the deck link; they do not by themselves prove that a real task or reply is available.
